catalog_quote: [Laycock 1969:78, page image] Stress is probably phonemic, if the evidence of P íbal 'quickly'/ipáy 'south' is trustworthy. Nevertheless, by far the most common stress placement is on the first syllable beginning with a consonant; accordingly, stress is marked only when this is not the case. [Verstraete 2019:282-283] stress patterns in Mbarrumbathama depend on three parameters: (i) the distinction between roots and compound structures, and within roots, (ii) the size of the root and (iii) the nature of the initial element. ... The majority of roots are consonant-initial, but there is a significant portion of vowel-initial roots (about 20 percent). ... Both the size of the root and the nature of its initial element have an influence on the stress pattern. audit.reasoning: Quote check: both deciding passages are present verbatim at the stated locators in copies we hold (Laycock p.78 page scan; Verstraete 2019 pp.282-283 in /txt). Identity: Laycock's 'L' is Capell Y78 Lamalama (p.71) and Verstraete 2019 describes the Mbarrumbathama clan variety of Lamalama (ISO lby = lamu1254), so both sources are on the right languoid; the only caveat is that Laycock's stress sentence is a joint statement for L, P and U with its 'phonemic' example drawn from P (Rimanggudinhma), which the record could note but which does not affect the classification since Verstraete 2019 independently gives the Lamalama-specific facts. Deciding source is a 2019 JIPA Illustration by the language's main documenter — the best available and. Glottolog lists no grammar, and the only unheld items (Verstraete 2023 Oxford Guide overview, Sommer's unpublished 61-pp sketch) could at most refine.
